key_insight: Adam achieves provable geometric decay of empirical training loss for sufficiently wide two-layer networks, including physics-informed neural networks solving the Poisson equation, under explicit parameter conditions.
engineering_relevance: The analysis clarifies how network width, Adam parameters, and minibatch size affect convergence guarantees for neural PDE solvers.
method: Use a Lyapunov function to control momentum in full-batch Adam.
Analyze minibatch Adam through exact virtual iterates, gradient–preconditioner dependence, and second-moment concentration.
Extend the theory to Poisson PINNs with separately sampled interior and boundary points.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports theoretical convergence guarantees, with minibatch loss decay established in restricted expectation on a high-probability event; it reports no numerical benchmarks.
watch_item: The guarantees require sufficiently wide two-layer networks and explicit Adam parameter conditions; empirical loss convergence does not alone establish PDE solution accuracy.
paper_title: On the Global Convergence of Stochastic Adam for Physics-Informed Neural Networks
